title: Bubble Watch
briefing: Pebble Games is the stock everyone is talking about. Orchard Foods is the stock nobody is talking about. One of them is about to teach a hard lesson.
objective: Recognize a hype bubble: keep size small, exit when it cracks, and do not buy the bounce.
debrief: Hype headlines on days 6, 10 and 14 pushed Pebble Games far above any measure of its profits. On day 19 it reversed on record volume, and the share-sale filing on day 20 started a collapse. A brief bounce on day 27 trapped late buyers before the slide resumed. Orchard Foods climbed slowly all the way. A disciplined player rode the hype with limited size, left on the reversal and kept the core in the steady stock.

assets.name: Pebble Games
assets.blurb: Makes console and mobile video games.

assets.name: Orchard Foods
assets.blurb: Runs a chain of neighborhood grocery stores.

news.headline: Pebble Games clip goes viral
news.body: A short clip of its next game has been shared millions of times.

news.headline: Forums crown Pebble Games "stock of the year"
news.body: Posts predict the shares will double again. None cite company figures.

news.headline: A celebrity says they bought Pebble Games shares
news.body: The post drew millions of views overnight.

news.headline: Pebble Games hits a record, then reverses on record volume
news.body: Heavy selling arrived in the afternoon.

news.headline: Pebble Games files to sell new shares at the high price
news.body: The company will raise cash by issuing more stock, diluting existing owners.

news.headline: "Buy the dip," say Pebble Games fans
news.body: Forum posts urge holders to buy more. Nothing about the business has changed.

news.headline: Analysts say Pebble Games is still expensive after the fall
news.body: Even after the drop, the shares trade far above similar studios.

bonus.text: Be out of Pebble Games by day 22
Do not buy the bounce (days 26 to 29)
Keep a core position in Orchard Foods from day 5 to day 35
